name: NVR Essentials
headline: One course. Your whole team using NVR.
intro: Non-violent resistance training that helps your whole team respond as one when a young person's behaviour escalates.
glance: 6 hours in person, or 2 hours live online

problem.scene: 11pm. A young person is kicking the office door.
problem.question: What does your team do next?
with: The same response on every shift
Resist the behaviour, never the child
problem.standards: The Children's Homes Regulations and the Fostering National Minimum Standards expect de-escalation. Neither says what to say at 11pm. This course does.
problem.evidence: Honest about the evidence: early trials with parents are encouraging, research in care settings is still limited, and we say so on the day.

groups: Support workers, team leaders, registered managers
Carers, supervising social workers, team leaders
Deciding whether NVR fits your service

outcomes: Describe an escalation from the young person's side and the adult's, and how shouting or backing off feeds it.
Sort behaviours into those to resist, those to negotiate and those to let go.
Explain non-violent resistance (Haim Omer, 2004), the seven pillars and the three dimensions of adult presence.
Show how NVR supports the Children's Homes Regulations and Standard 3 of the Fostering National Minimum Standards.
Use cold-iron lines, delayed responses and baskets in a hot moment.
Plan a reconciliation gesture, an act of resistance and a first NVR session for your team.
story_line: One story runs through the day: Reece, 15, in a children's home. Reece is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

parts.title: The NVR stance
parts.story: Reece kicks the door until the Wi-Fi stays on.
parts.theory: From control to presence: the seven pillars.
parts.action: Map the cycle. Drop one habit.
parts.leave: The NVR framework on one page

parts.title: De-escalation
parts.story: 10:55pm. Reece waits to see what the adult does.
parts.theory: Strike when the iron is cold.
parts.action: Practise cold-iron lines. Sort the baskets.

parts.title: Reconciliation and resistance
parts.story: The next morning: his favourite toast.
parts.theory: Resist the behaviour, never the child.
parts.action: Build a gesture menu. Rehearse an announcement.
parts.leave: A gesture menu and a resistance plan

parts.title: Leading it in your team
parts.story: Six weeks on, every shift responds the same way.
parts.action: Map supporters. Plan your first team session.
parts.leave: A plan for your first team session
